rgb: An indoor checkout counter is positioned immediately in front of and below the camera wearer, approximately 0.4 to 0.8 metres away, with a glass display case farther behind it on the right at around 1.8 to 2.5 metres. On the counter, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person across from them, a black cash register with its drawer open occupies the left-centre (about 0.5 metres away), next to a dark jar and brown bag at the far left. On the right are an upright brown paper bag (about 0.6 metres away) and, to its right, a red plastic basket (about 0.8 metres away), separated from one another by roughly 0.1 to 0.3 metres. From left to right through the five frames, the camera angles slightly upward and moves slightly backward in frame 5, revealing the lower half of the person's face, still oriented toward the camera wearer, and a stack of banknotes along the bottom edge beside the register, while cutting off the bottom of the register keypad. At the same time, the person's right hand moves slightly forward and downward over the open drawer.
depth: The depth map shows a checkout counter immediately in front of and beneath the camera wearer. A cash register at bottom-left, a tall brown paper bag at centre-right, a jar at the far bottom-left, and a red basket at the far right appear brightly in the foreground, roughly 0.4–0.8 m away and within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person on the opposite side. A person stands behind the register on the upper-left, approximately 0.9–1.2 m from the camera wearer and facing toward them, about 0.3–0.5 m behind the register and beside the paper bag. Farther back, a display case occupies the upper-right at roughly 1.8–2.5 m. The person's lower body is partly hidden by the register and counter edge. In frames 1–4, the top of their head is clipped by the upper image boundary; it becomes partially visible in frame 5 when the camera tilts slightly upward and the person leans slightly forward, extending both hands downward toward the register drawer. Relative to RGB alone, the depth view distinctly separates the recessed cash drawer from the register's elevated keypad housing and emphasizes the hollow internal depth of both the open paper bag and the red basket. Its estimates nevertheless appear unreliable in the dark background opening between the person and paper bag, where depth collapses into uniform black, and across the flat countertop paper beneath the bag, which merges gradually with the bag's base instead of forming a crisp depth boundary.
segmentation: Across the five frames, the instance segmentation map detects only a limited portion of the scene. The person behind the counter on the upper-left, 0.9–1.2 m away and facing the camera wearer, is segmented only in frames 2, 4, and 5. Foreground items at 0.4–0.8 m, all reachable by both people, are detected intermittently and assigned incorrect classes. In particular, the far-left jar is marked as 'bottle' in frame 1 and 'cup' in frame 5; the lower-left cash register is called 'laptop' in frame 1 and divided into 'keyboard' and 'book' in frame 2; the tall brown paper bag to the register's right is classified as 'book' throughout frames 1–4; the cash notes at bottom-centre are labelled 'cup' in frame 1; and the background display case on the upper-right, 1.8–2.5 m away, is labelled 'tv' in frame 5. Over the sequence, the masks follow the slight upward camera tilt by frame 5, adding more of the person's upper torso and neck to the mask while the right-side paper bag disappears from segmentation altogether. They also represent the register occluding the person's lower torso in frames 2 and 4. Although the segmentation produces crisp exterior outlines of the person's shoulders and torso against the dark background, where RGB contrast is weak, both its classifications and frame-to-frame consistency are highly unreliable: it entirely omits the person in frames 1 and 3 and never detects the red basket at the far right.
pose: The pose map follows the skeleton and hands of the lone person behind the counter on the upper-left, roughly 0.9–1.2 m from the camera wearer. The person faces directly toward the camera wearer, with both hands located within arm's reach of the cash register drawer, which is 0.5–0.8 m from the camera wearer and immediately left of the paper bag. Because the person's head is largely cropped by the top image edge and the register blocks their waist in frames 1–4, the map identifies only the raised right hand, shown in magenta and hovering just over the open cash drawer. Frame 1 also contains a false-positive tiny yellow body skeleton on the far-left jar. From frames 1 through 4, the right hand moves slightly downward and toward the right within the frame as the camera view tilts upward. In frame 5, once the person's head enters the image, a complete upper-body skeleton appears, including the shoulders, torso, both arms, and five facial keypoints along the top edge; both hands extend down into the register drawer approximately 0.2 m apart. Compared with the motion-blurred RGB frames, the pose view reveals the precise 2D finger-joint articulation of the right hand and the symmetrical, forward-facing shoulder alignment in frame 5 much more clearly. However, it remains unreliable in frames 1–4, completely missing the visible torso, arms, and left hand resting against the register's side, while also hallucinating the miniature jar skeleton in frame 1.
